therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Type 2 diabetes patients for whom metformin is inappropriate
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: HbA1c change from baseline at week 18

results.effect_size: -0.60% HbA1c change from baseline (linagliptin vs placebo, final analysis)
biomarker_changes: FPG change from baseline at week 18: linagliptin -13.3 mg/dL vs placebo +7.2 mg/dL (interim analysis), difference -20.5 mg/dL, p=0.0002
HbA1c <7.0% at week 18: 23.5% linagliptin vs 11.8% placebo (OR 2.576, p=0.0374)
HbA1c <6.5% at week 18: 8.9% linagliptin vs 2.9% placebo (OR 3.285, p=0.1281)
HbA1c lowering ≥0.5% at week 18: 36.1% linagliptin vs 17.8% placebo (OR 2.801, p=0.0046)
After placebo switch to glimepiride (week 22+), HbA1c reductions in glimepiride arm converged toward and exceeded linagliptin arm
subgroup_findings: HbA1c change at week 52: linagliptin -0.44% vs glimepiride -0.72%
FPG change at week 52: linagliptin -14.0 mg/dL vs glimepiride -19.1 mg/dL
safety_signals: Acute myocardial infarction: 1 event in placebo/glimepiride arm (1/76)
Myocardial infarction: 1 event in linagliptin arm (1/151)
Colon cancer: 1 event in placebo/glimepiride arm (1/76)
Cerebral infarction: 1 event in placebo/glimepiride arm (1/76)

context.comparator: Placebo (part 1, weeks 1–18); Glimepiride 1–4 mg (part 2, weeks 19–52, former placebo patients)

results_by_chain.population_description: Type 2 diabetes patients for whom metformin is inappropriate
